H01.title: Medieval Merchant’s House, Southampton
H01.basis: Home, shop and workplace in one medieval property.

H02.title: Medieval Shop from Horsham
H02.basis: Paired shops, possible upstairs residence and rear production/hearth space; reconstruction uncertainty recorded by museum.

H03.title: People in Place, 1550–1720
H03.basis: Early-modern comparison for lodgers, multiple households, apprentices and servants; not medieval demographic calibration.

H04.title: Medieval hospitals and almshouses
H04.basis: Charitable residential care and shared infirmary spaces, distinct from ordinary worker housing.

H05.title: Rievaulx Abbey teaching kit
H05.basis: Institutional dormitory/refectory/service ranges; not evidence of general labourer barracks.

H06.title: Goodrich Castle household
H06.basis: Castle households include officers and service workers as well as a ruling family.

H07.title: Bayleaf farmstead
H07.basis: Hall, service rooms, upper private chamber and productive gardens; displayed setting circa 1540.

H08.title: Warkworth significance
H08.basis: Long rear gardens preserve earlier town property divisions.

H09.title: Merchant Adventurers’ Hall undercroft
H09.basis: Guild institution with a charitable accommodation component.

H10.title: Medieval churches in York
H10.basis: Multiple parish churches, monastic institutions and chapels within one city.

H11.title: Richmond Castle teaching resource
H11.basis: Defensible high ground and control of a river crossing.

H12.title: Life in a castle
H12.basis: Fortress as home and workplace as well as military installation.

H13.title: Farm buildings at Weald & Downland
H13.basis: Functional farm-building categories; displayed structures span periods, so individual forms need dating.

H14.title: Commerce and exchange buildings
H14.basis: Broad commerce/market/inn categories spanning periods; not validation of every proposed medieval subtype.

H15.title: London is a shoemaking city
H15.basis: Shoemaking as an important medieval urban trade.

H16.title: High Ousegate archaeological report
H16.basis: Excavated leatherworking evidence in Anglo-Scandinavian York; earlier comparison, not a universal city recipe.

R01.title: Vanegas et al., Interactive Design of Urban Spaces (2009)
R01.basis: Coupling population/jobs with parcels/buildings; modern urban model, independent medieval adaptation proposed.
